chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Ibn Muni'a narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shoyba narrated to us, saying: Abu Muawiyah narrated from Al-A'amash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, saying:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, among the worst of people near God, the Exalted and Mighty, on the Day of Resurrection are the two-faced ones.'

key_terms.ذُو الْوَجْهَيْنِ: The two-faced one (one who shows one face to a group and another to a different group, indicating hypocrisy or inconsistency)
key_terms.عِنْدَ اللَّهِ: In the sight of God / Near God

ai.seo_question: Who are considered the worst of people on the Day of Resurrection according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the 'two-faced' (dhā al-wajhayn) as among the worst of people, emphasizing the severity of hypocrisy where one displays different faces to different groups. This concept is deeply rooted in Shia ethical tradition, warning against the moral corruption of saying one thing to the face and another behind it, a trait that alienates the believer from divine favor. The hadith serves as a practical guide for maintaining sincerity (ikhlas) in both private and public spheres.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-17 Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated that Ibn Muni’a quoted on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shoyba’, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, on the authority of Al-A’amash, on the authority of Abi Salih, on the authority of Abi Hurayrih that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “
The worst of thepeople near the Honorable the Exalted God on the Resurrection Day are the two-faced ones.”
